__comment: Privy policy engine — signing-layer backstop (the Stripe/Privy analogue of Coinbase CDP's policy). Privy policies are attached per-wallet via the wallet's policy_ids, and are FAIL-CLOSED: within a method, a signing request that matches no ALLOW rule is denied, and an unlisted method defaults to DENY. x402's EVM 'exact' scheme signs an EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization as EIP-712 typed data via eth_signTypedData_v4, so the rule matches the typed-data message fields: 'to' as a recipient allowlist (operator in_condition_set, referencing a condition set of approved payTo addresses) and 'value' as a per-transaction cap (operator lte, USDC base units with 6 decimals), plus the domain chainId to pin the chain (Base Sepolia 84532). CRITICAL: the 'types' map below must match the signing request's typed data EXACTLY — if it does not, the condition evaluates to FALSE (it does not skip). For a fail-closed ALLOW rule a mismatch simply denies the payment (safe); for a DENY-based denylist a mismatch would let the request through (unsafe). This is the failure observed in the AgentCore Payments pentest (OFAC denylist on 'to' did not fire). Prefer this ALLOW-allowlist shape over a denylist. Matching is also case-sensitive, so include both the lowercase and checksummed casing of every address in the condition set. Docs: https://docs.privy.io/controls/policies
name: x402 recipient allowlist and per-tx cap
owner_id: <optional-owner-id — set in production so the app secret alone cannot edit the policy>

rules.name: Allow x402 USDC transfer to an approved recipient under the cap on Base Sepolia
